quote: I know we have a couple different options. To be honest, I'm not exactly sure what options they are, just because I'm I'm just like a scheduler. I'm not a scheduler by any means.
stewart_read: The rep is reaching for the scope-limitation escape hatch but executes it so haltingly (self-contradicting mid-sentence) that it reads as evasive rather than confident redirection.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as strategic scope-holding, but the stammering and self-correction ('I'm not a scheduler by any means') undercuts that — this is an in-the-moment knowledge gap, not a deployed strategy.
coaching_implication: Coach the clean version of the escape hatch: acknowledge the question is important, state plainly that the specialist covers exact payoff terms, and pivot to the appointment with confidence — not mid-sentence backpedaling.

quote: So on the average, do you happen to know how long it's the average cost of the panels?
stewart_read: Second time the customer asks for cost/timeline specifics; rep's response ('I don't I') is an incomplete non-answer rather than a redirect.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive — no evidence rep intended to loop back to this later; the conversation moves straight to booking mechanics instead.
coaching_implication: This is the second touch of the same unanswered question — flag as a pattern, not an isolated miss, when reviewing with the rep.

quote: is there anything gonna be done if there is is there a leak protection for the roof with this program?
stewart_read: Customer raises a concrete, checkable concern (roof leak warranty) that is a natural curiosity/trust anchor for the appointment, but rep's answer ('tons of warranties and everything') is vague and generic rather than tied forward to what the closer will show him.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to convert specific concerns like this into a reason to attend the appointment ('that's exactly the kind of detail the specialist walks through on your specific roof') rather than a vague reassurance.

quote: As long as the bill there's nothing upfront that we have to pay as far as the installation, that would be more open to doing.
stewart_read: This is the customer stating his core condition for moving forward — essentially a soft objection wrapped in a conditional. The rep does not acknowledge or confirm it at all before moving to lock the time.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive miss — there's no later moment in the call where the rep circles back to confirm no-upfront-cost, so this wasn't deferred strategically.
coaching_implication: This is the single most consequential missed line in the call — the customer told the rep exactly what he needs to hear to stay engaged, and it went unconfirmed. Replay this exact clip with the rep.

quote: do you have a copy of your Mecklenburg bill with your kilowatt usage on it?
stewart_read: Rep names an incorrect/unrelated utility company, confusing the customer, who has to ask 'Are you with Dominion?' back at the rep — a basic data error at the verify stage.
coaching_implication: Simple process fix: confirm utility company by asking, don't assume or misstate it. Small error but it cost credibility right before the bill-collection ask.

quote: Now, it'll just be me. My wife goes to work on Wednesdays.
stewart_read: Customer discloses his wife will not be present and won't listen to the call ('She don't wanna listen to the conversation... She'd rather just read the paperwork herself'). Rep acknowledges but does not attempt to find a time that works for both or flag this for the closer as a co-owner gap.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as customer declining on the spouse's behalf, which the rep can't override — but schema calls for at least offering an alternative time for both to be on the call, which never happens.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always float the joint-time option per protocols.spouse_decision, even if the customer ultimately declines — right now the rep skips straight to accepting solo attendance.

quote: You said you already sent the text? ... Yeah. I just barely sent it. So it should be, honestly, over to you.
stewart_read: Call ends without the rep restating the appointment day/time, the one-hour block, no-driving/computer expectation, or a clean 'is that fair?' handshake — it just trails off into pleasantries after confusion over whether the text was sent.
coaching_implication: Coach a clean button-up close: even after the awkward text-confirmation moment, the rep should recap Wednesday 2:30, the hour block, and get an explicit yes before signing off.
